presentingComplaint: Spreading redness, swelling and pain of the left lower leg for 4 days, worsening despite oral antibiotics.
history: Type 2 diabetic on metformin. Noticed a small area of redness over the left shin after minor gardening trauma. GP started oral flucloxacillin 500 mg QDS 3 days ago, but the erythema has continued to advance up the leg and a small area has begun to weep pus. Reports subjective fevers and rigors since yesterday. Had a boil on the same leg drained 2 months ago that grew MRSA, and he received a short oral antibiotic course then. No calf pain on immobility, no recent long-haul travel, no shortness of breath. Denies rapidly worsening agonising pain, skin blistering or crackling. No prior venous ulceration. Non-smoker.
examination: Alert, mildly unwell but not confused. Left lower leg from mid-shin to just below the knee is warm, tender, oedematous with confluent erythema and ill-defined, non-raised borders; the advancing margin has been marked and has extended 2 cm overnight. A 1.5 cm superficial pustular focus over the shin is expressing purulent material. No crepitus, no haemorrhagic bullae, tenderness proportionate to visible inflammation. Tender left inguinal lymphadenopathy. Peripheral pulses palpable; no calf induration or cords. No track marks.
imaging: Bedside point-of-care ultrasound of the affected area: subcutaneous oedema with 'cobblestoning' consistent with cellulitis; a small (1 cm) hypoechoic collection beneath the pustular focus amenable to drainage. No deep fascial fluid, no gas. Doppler shows no DVT.
microbiology: Pus from drained focus and blood cultures sent. Gram stain of pus: Gram-positive cocci in clusters. Culture at 48h: Staphylococcus aureus, methicillin-resistant (MRSA); sensitive to vancomycin, linezolid, doxycycline and co-trimoxazole; resistant to flucloxacillin/oxacillin and erythromycin. Blood cultures no growth.
differentialDiagnoses: Necrotizing fasciitis (excluded: no pain out of proportion, crepitus, bullae or systemic toxicity)
Erysipelas (less likely: borders ill-defined and non-raised, deeper involvement)
Diabetic foot infection (lesion is on shin, not foot ulcer)
finalDiagnosis: Purulent cellulitis of the left lower leg due to methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), failing empirical beta-lactam therapy, with a small drainable collection.
citations: IDSA - Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Skin and Soft Tissue Infections - 2014
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e - Cellulitis and Soft-Tissue Infections
stewardship: This is purulent cellulitis that has progressed despite an adequately dosed anti-streptococcal/anti-MSSA beta-lactam (flucloxacillin), in a patient with documented prior MRSA. Purulence plus beta-lactam failure plus prior MRSA mandates escalation to MRSA-active therapy: admit for IV vancomycin (weight-based, trough/AUC-guided). Source control is essential - incise and drain the localised collection and send pus for culture; drainage is the primary intervention for purulent SSTI. Once susceptibilities confirm MRSA and the patient is afebrile/improving, de-escalate to an oral MRSA-active agent (doxycycline, co-trimoxazole, or clindamycin) to complete a 5-7 day course. Continued anti-pseudomonal/Gram-negative cover is NOT indicated. Optimise glycaemic control as an adjunct.
contraindications: Avoid nephrotoxins and monitor renal function and vancomycin levels (AUC/trough) given diabetes and IV glycopeptide use
Do not continue flucloxacillin alone once MRSA is confirmed - it is intrinsically resistant
Avoid empirical broad Gram-negative/anti-pseudomonal cover in the absence of risk factors - unnecessary escalation
edgeCases: If pain becomes out of proportion, or crepitus/haemorrhagic bullae/rapid systemic deterioration develop → urgent surgical review to exclude necrotizing fasciitis
Failure to improve at 48-72h despite MRSA cover → re-image for an undrained/enlarging abscess requiring repeat source control
Bilateral lower-limb erythema without a portal of entry should prompt reconsideration of a non-infective mimic (venous stasis, lipodermatosclerosis)
expectedMaiK: Purulent cellulitis progressing despite an anti-MSSA beta-lactam, in a patient with prior MRSA, requires escalation to MRSA-active therapy (IV vancomycin) PLUS incision and drainage of any collection, with culture-directed de-escalation to an oral MRSA agent.
expectedNextQuestions: Any prior MRSA-positive cultures, colonisation or recent boils/abscesses?
Which antibiotic, dose and duration has already been given and what was the response?
Is there fluctuance or a collection suggesting an abscess that needs drainage?
Any red flags for necrotizing infection - pain out of proportion, crepitus, bullae, or systemic toxicity?
expectedInvestigations: Incision & drainage with pus for Gram stain and culture/sensitivity
CBC with differential, CRP, renal function and glucose/HbA1c
Point-of-care ultrasound to detect a drainable collection and exclude DVT

investigations: Incision & drainage with pus culture and sensitivity

regressionAssertions: Empiric regimen must be MRSA-active (vancomycin) given purulence, prior MRSA and beta-lactam failure
Management must include source control (incision & drainage) of the collection
Plan must specify culture-directed de-escalation to an oral MRSA agent once improving
Necrotizing fasciitis must remain a differential but be excluded on absence of pain out of proportion, crepitus and bullae
